prs.title: fix(semantic): stop arguments resolution at ordinary functions
prs.author: camc314

prs.title: perf(linter/oxc/bad-array-method-on-arguments): check arguments references once
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Inspect unresolved `arguments` references once per file instead of running on every static and computed member expression. Also check references bound to bare `var arguments;` declarations in ordinary functions, since those declarations retain the implicit arguments object. Parameters, lexical bindings, initialized declarations, and loop bindings remain excluded.

The standard fixture call count drops from 94,090 to 7, one invocation per file. Depends on the semantic fix in #26929 through #26933.

prs.title: fix(ci): request pull-requests permission for monitor and ecosystem CI tokens
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
## Summary

#27476 scoped the GitHub App tokens in `monitor-oxc.yml` and `ecosystem-ci.yml` to `actions: write` + `issues: write`. The oxc-guard installation does not grant `issues`, so creating the token now fails, and with it the whole trigger job ([failed run on #26929](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/actions/runs/38191638085/job/114625444599?pr=26929)):

```
Failed to create token for "oxc-project/oxc,oxc-project/monitor-oxc":
The permissions requested are not granted to this installation. (422)
```

Before #27476 the step requested no specific permissions, so the token got everything the installation has, and `issues` was never checked. When specific permissions are named, GitHub rejects the whole request if any one is missing.

Both workflows use the token only to list, create and update comments and to remove a label on the triggering PR. GitHub accepts the `pull-requests` permission for those calls on a PR, and the app already has it: the old workflow commented on PRs without `issues`, and other workflows request `pull-requests: write` from the same app. This PR requests `pull-requests: write` in place of `issues: write` and keeps the narrow scope from #27476.

`ecosystem-ci.yml` has had the same pair since #27476 but hasn't run for real since, so it would fail the same way on the next `run-ox*-ecosystem-ci` label.

## Notes

- `actions: write` stays as it is. It's needed to dispatch `monitor-oxc` / `oxc-ecosystem-ci`, and the app already has it, because those disp

prs.title: fix(minifier): preserve parameter writes through mapped arguments
prs.author: Dunqing

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic `type` reads
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of [#27458](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27458).

Avoid reading `type` of a node multiple times where the node can have multiple object shapes. In such a case, loading `.type` is a megamorphic property access, which is expensive, and V8 does not cache the result.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic `type` reads in `printMemberExpression`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of [#27458](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27458).

The object of a computed member expression can be any expression, so reading its `type` is a megamorphic load (a builtin call, which V8 does not deduplicate). Read its `type` once for the `(let)[0]` check, while unwrapping parens, instead of in `withoutParens` and again after it.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce branches in `printObjectProperty`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

Move a branch which depends on `!computed` into inside an existing branch which already has that check, removing the 2nd branch on that condition.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): ensure `shorthand` var is always a boolean
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Tiny perf optimization.

Ensure that V8 can prove that `shorthand` is always a boolean, and can avoid a type check when branching on it later on.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic `type` reads in `printObjectProperty`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of [#27458](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27458).

A property's value can be any expression, so reading its `type` is a megamorphic load (a builtin call, which V8 does not deduplicate). Read it once, and reuse it for the method check (twice in TS builds) and the shorthand check, instead of reading it again in `withoutParens` and after it.

Ditto for the load of `type` property on `key` in the `!computed` branch.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic `type` reads in `printConditionalExpression`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of [#27458](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27458).

The test of a conditional expression can be any expression, so reading its `type` is a megamorphic load (a builtin call, which V8 does not deduplicate). In TS builds, read its `type` once while unwrapping parens, instead of in `withoutParens` and again after it.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic `type` reads in `printDirectivesAndStatements`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of [#27458](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27458).

The expression of a leading expression statement can be any expression, so reading its `type` is a megamorphic load (a builtin call, which V8 does not deduplicate). Read its `type` once while unwrapping parens, instead of in `withoutParens` and again after it.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic `type` reads in `printForOfStatement`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of [#27458](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27458).

The left side of a `for of` head can be any declaration or assignment target, so reading its `type` is a megamorphic load (a builtin call, which V8 does not deduplicate). Read it once in `printForOfStatement` and pass it to a single `forOfHeadNeedsWrapping`, which applies both the `let` and `async` rules while walking the leftmost spine, reading each level's `type` once.

Previously computed members read their object's `type` three times (via `withoutParens`). Adds a fixture and hand-built tests for `let`/`async` heads, including parenthesized ones, which only hand-built ASTs can reach.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce writes in `printForOfStatement`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

Combine writes when printing a `ForOfStatement`. Previous it was 2 writes (`for`, ` (`) or 3 (`for`, ` await`, ` (`). Now either is just one write.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic `type` reads in `printParams`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of [#27458](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27458).

In TS builds, a parameter can be any of several node types, so reading its `type` is a megamorphic load (a builtin call, which V8 does not deduplicate). Read it once for both the `this` parameter and parameter property checks.

prs.title: refactor(packages/codegen): remove `UnknownNode` type
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Refactor. Remove the `UnknownNode` type, which was a hack to satisfy the type-checker. It made function signatures misleading. Replace it by another mechanism which achieves the same thing, but has tighter typing.

It was this change which revealed the lack of support for printing `V8IntrinsicExpression`s (fixed in #27597).

prs.title: fix(packages/codegen): support printing `V8IntrinsicExpression`s
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body: `oxc_codegen` (Rust) supports printing `V8IntrinsicExpression`s but `oxc-codegen` (JS) didn't. Add support for it.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): print `SpreadElement` arguments via `printExpression`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of [#27458](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27458).

An argument can be any expression, so reading its `type` is a megamorphic load (a builtin call, which V8 does not deduplicate). `printArguments` read it to check for a spread, and then `printExpression` read it again to dispatch. Add a `SpreadElement` arm to `printExpression`, so arguments are passed straight to it, and their `type` is read only once.

This change produces a 1%-1.5% perf improvement on most benchamarks.

perf(packages/codegen): remove unnecessary `printSpaceBeforeIdentifier` calls
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

Remove unnecessary `printSpaceBeforeIdentifier` calls in `printAssignmentTargetProperty`. The last thing printed is always either `{` or `, `, so `printSpaceBeforeIdentifier` is always a no-op here anyway.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce branches in `printArguments`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Small perf optimization.

The loop always checks if `length === 0` anyway before first iteration, so there's no real gain in checking it manually.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): remove branch printing `RestElement` in `ArrayPattern`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

When printing `...rest` in an `ArrayPattern`, there's no need to send it via `printBindingPattern` which checks `rest.type`. We already know it's a `RestElement`, so just print that directly.

prs.title: fix(codegen, packages/codegen): remove extraneous space before `RestElement` in `ArrayPattern`
prs.author: overlookmotel

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): remove branches from loops printing arrays
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

Optimize printing arrays - `ArrayExpression` and `ArrayPattern`.

- Move branches out of the loops, so each loop iteration is as quick as possible.
- Convert `write` calls to `writeNoLast` wherever possible.

prs.title: fix(linter/sort-keys): compare natural order like ESLint
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
`sort-keys` with `natural: true` disagreed with ESLint. It reported correctly sorted objects such as `{ a12, a100 }`, `{ item1Name, item10Name }` and `{ "/user/list", "/user-list" }`. Its comparator was also not a total order (`a12 > a100 > a20 > a12`), so sorting for the fix could panic.

The comparator is now a port of ESLint's `natural-compare`: UTF-16 code units in its character order, with digit runs compared by numeric value. The fix now sorts stably, so it no longer swaps duplicate keys in objects with more than 20 properties, which changed which value wins. Every rule test agrees with ESLint 10.1.0.

Two documented differences remain: case-insensitive mode lowercases ASCII only, and digit runs beyond 2^53 compare exactly.

Part of #26242.

Implemented with AI assistance.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_0123ytJDyebxiELUzaFc1nwd

fix(ecmascript): do not fold `Math.cbrt` of a negative number to `NaN`
prs.author: baltasarblanco
prs.body:
### Bug

`Math.cbrt` of a negative constant is folded to `NaN` (oxc-minify 0.153.0, default options; same output on `main` at 9a9eb83):

```js
console.log(Math.cbrt(-8), Math.cbrt(-1), Math.cbrt(-Infinity));
// before: console.log(NaN,NaN,NaN)   -> NaN NaN NaN
// after:  console.log(-2,-1,-1/0)    -> -2 -1 -Infinity
```

It also happens through a constant (`const n = -8; Math.cbrt(n)` → `NaN`), and for non-integral results (`Math.cbrt(-2)` → `NaN`).

`try_fold_roots` (`crates/oxc_ecmascript/src/constant_evaluation/call_expr.rs`, added in #8731) handles `sqrt` and `cbrt` together and returns `NaN` for every `arg < 0` before looking at the name. That is right for [`Math.sqrt`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-math.sqrt) ("If n < -0𝔽, return NaN") but not for [`Math.cbrt`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-math.cbrt), which returns `n` itself when it is not finite (so `-Infinity` for `-Infinity`) and otherwise the cube root of `n`, which is negative for a negative `n`.

### Fix

- The early `NaN` return now applies only to `sqrt`.
- `Math.cbrt(-Infinity)` folds to `-Infinity`.
- Other negative arguments go through `f64::cbrt` with the existing `fract() == 0.0` check, so `Math.cbrt(-8)` folds to `-2` and `Math.cbrt(-2)` is left as is (same policy as for positive arguments).

### Tests

Added to `test_fold_math_functions_cbrt` (`crates/oxc_minifier/tests/peephole/replace_known_methods.rs`): `Math.cbrt(-1)` → `-1`, `Math.cbrt(-8)` → `-2`, `Math.cbrt(-Infinity)` → `-Infinity`, and `Math.cbr
…(truncated)
